alex: Heads-up — seeing a regression on host-side streaming after the kernel-selector change. Short streams (<=64 tokens) p99 up ~10-25%.

sara: ugh. which part of the host path? tokenization? framing?

alex: traced it to the token demux + small-write path. Flamegraph shows a lot of time in hostcodec::demux -> writev -> grpc_send. Extra copies and syscall bursts.

matt: that matches a KV cache eviction spike I saw for the same window. Small writes are causing the writev to split at bad boundaries, hitting tcp Nagle + grpc layer overhead.

julia: did the kernel selector change alter coalescing hints?

alex: yes — selector now prefers 'kernel_fastpath' for short sequences which accidentally disabled small-chunk coalescing. Perf trace attached: https://perf.company/reports/176752-demux-flame.svg (flame shows per-request syscalls rising). infra-bot also logged request traces for 1767523456.

sara: can you paste the minimal repro or the perf record?

alex: perf record snippet (shortened):
```
  #0  writev
  #1  grpc_perform_send
  #2  hostcodec::demux::emit_chunk
  #3  request_handler::stream_iterate
```

alex: quick local patch that coalesces tiny chunks before hitting writev — cut p99 back down in my canary run. Patch: 
```diff
--- a/hostcodec/demux.cpp
+++ b/hostcodec/demux.cpp
@@ -42,6 +42,11 @@
-  buffer.append(chunk);
+  // coalesce tiny fragments to avoid writev syscall thrash
+  if (chunk.size() < 256 && buffer.tail_size() < 1024) {
+    buffer.coalesce_inplace(chunk);
+  } else {
+    buffer.append(chunk);
+  }
```

matt: nice. any kvcache interactions? coalescing should reduce KV lookups per token burst.

alex: yes, after patch KV eviction rate drops ~18% in the canary and we see fewer spike bursts in kvcache.hits.miss.

perf-bot: canary metrics (5% traffic, 30m): p50 120ms -> 118ms, p95 280ms -> 260ms, p99 480ms -> 370ms. CPU sys time down ~12%.

julia: strong evidence. I'm +1 to revert the kernel-selector change that disabled the coalescing hint and keep this patch. We need a microbench to prevent regressions.

sara: agree. create a follow-up ticket for microbench and add an assertion in the selector unit tests to preserve coalescing hints for short streams.

alex: opened ticket RNDF-1218. Will propose revert PR for kernel-selector and include the demux coalesce patch as a hotfix. Scheduling rollback window tomorrow 11:00 PST if no objections.

matt: FYI — also saw minor HTTP/1.1 edge-case: with some clients the chunk boundaries cause header flushes; adding coalesce reduces header churn too.

infra-bot: deploy/174 created (canary 5%), patch applied to hostcodec service.

julia: thanks — keep monitoring. If perf-bot shows stable numbers at 12h we'll promote. :thumbsup:

alex: will follow-up with flamegraphs and the microbench plan. Thanks all.
